Article Title: 'Discussions ended the day he left us': Supriya Sule breaks silence on NCP merger buzz
Article Text:
Supriya Sule's message on NCP merger after Ajit Pawar's death

NEW DELHI: Nationalist Congress Party (SP) working president and MP Supriya Sule on Saturday said discussions over a possible merger between the two rival NCP factions had come to an end following the death of her brother and former Maharashtra deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar Her remarks come amid speculation over a possible reunion between the factions led by Sharad Pawar and Ajit Pawar, with leaders from both sides now ruling out any immediate merger.Speaking at a presser, Sule said, "The merger (of both factions of the party) was discussed until my brother (Ajit Pawar) was alive. The day he left us, it put a full stop to those discussions."Ajit Pawar died on January 28, 2026 after the aircraft carrying him crashed while attempting to land at Baramati airport in Pune district.Meanwhile, Maharashtra NCP president and MP Sunil Tatkare on Friday also dismissed speculation about a possible merger, asserting that his faction was not considering any reunion with the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SCP).“There is absolutely no discussion regarding a merger in our party at any level,” Tatkare told news agency ANI.Speculation over a possible reunion intensified after senior NCP leader Praful Patel recently met Sharad Pawar.However, Tatkare described the meeting as a personal visit to enquire about the veteran leader's health, dismissing any political significance.“Pawar Sahab has contributed to national politics for 60 years. At 86, his health hasn't been well. We have all reached various political positions with his blessings. Praful Bhai simply went to check on his health,” he said.Reaffirming his faction's association with the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA), Tatkare said, “We joined the NDA after deep consideration under the leadership of Narendra Modi. We are in the NDA and will remain in the NDA."Tatkare also hit back at Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut over his recent claim that 20 to 22 MLAs were ready to switch sides.“After the assembly elections, his mental health has deteriorated. Mentally, he is not fit. These statements are completely baseless,” he said.Tatkare further asserted that his faction would remain with the NDA under the leadership of Sunetra Pawar, adding that the "question of a merger does not even arise."Clarifying his earlier remarks on the merger discussions, Tatkare said there was "no confusion" on his part. He maintained that late Ajit Pawar, whom party leaders referred to as 'Dada', had spoken to him in detail about a possible merger on February 12 and had even outlined a formula for the arrangement after the proposed reunion.
Article Summary: Nationalist Congress Party (SP) working president and MP Supriya Sule said discussions over a possible merger between the two rival NCP factions had come to an end following the death of her brother Ajit Pawar. Sule: "The merger (of both factions of the party) was discussed until my brother (Ajit Pawar) was alive. The day he left us, it put a full stop to those discussions"

Article Title: Mekedatu Dam row: Stalin seeks united Tamil Nadu stand, asks Vijay to call all-party meeting
Article Text:
Stalin asks Vijay government not to remain silent on Mekedatu project

Stalin proposes joint meeting with PM Modi

Shivakumar says Karnataka will protect its right to build dam

NEW DELHI: DMK chief and former Tamil Nadu chief minister MK Stalin on Saturday urged chief minister Joseph Vijay to convene an all-party meeting to discuss Karnataka 's proposed Mekedatu dam project, calling for a united political response to protect the state's Cauvery water rights and the livelihood of its farmers.In a letter dated November 14, Stalin referred to Karnataka deputy chief minister DK Shivakumar 's recent remarks that no one could stop the construction of the proposed dam.Shivakumar made the statement at a government function in Mysuru on Friday in the presence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi .Sharing the letter on X, Stalin said Karnataka's position on the project required a response from the Tamil Nadu government. He described the Cauvery issue as a matter of "life and death" for the state and urged Vijay's government not to remain silent."Beyond mere water sharing, Cauvery is historically and emotionally intertwined with the lives of Tamils. The entire livelihood of delta farmers depends upon it," Stalin wrote.He said political parties in Karnataka were speaking in one voice on the Cauvery issue and argued that Tamil Nadu's parties should also demonstrate unity. Stalin had previously called for an all-party meeting to discuss the state's next steps, he said."Given the situation where the Karnataka Chief Minister has once again begun speaking aggressively about building the Mekedatu dam, the Government of Tamil Nadu must no longer remain silent. Therefore, I request through this letter that an all-party meeting be convened to express our unity and opposition to the Karnataka chief minister's statements," he wrote.Stalin also proposed that leaders of legislative parties in Tamil Nadu and all-party MPs jointly meet Prime Minister Modi to present the state's position.He said they should submit the resolutions adopted at the proposed all-party meeting, along with a unanimous resolution passed by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly against the Mekedatu project in June, directly to the Prime Minister."Regarding Cauvery rights, it is essential that we stand united, transcending personal likes and dislikes as well as party differences," Stalin said.The DMK leader also questioned reports that Vijay was planning to visit Karnataka for discussions on the Cauvery issue. He reiterated that Tamil Nadu's position had consistently been to secure its water rights through legal means rather than negotiations with Karnataka.Stalin said the state had previously warned against such a visit, quoting his earlier message to Vijay: "Do not run into this disaster."He also cited Shivakumar's remarks that it was the Tamil Nadu government which had sought talks, not Karnataka, and that the Tamil Nadu chief minister did not need to visit the neighbouring state under the present circumstances.The latest exchange follows Shivakumar's remarks on Friday, when he said Karnataka would protect its right to build the Mekedatu balancing reservoir and release 177 thousand million cubic feet (TMC) of water to Tamil Nadu as required by law.Shivakumar said the Supreme Court had already passed an order on the issue and that the next step was to secure the necessary clearances. He said he had sought forest and environmental approvals from the Centre."Mekedatu issue - Supreme Court has given order. Now what we need is just one thing - all parties have agreed, let's go together. For that, I am sending everything - forest clearance, environment clearance. I have asked for one forest clearance and one environment clearance," he said.Shivakumar maintained that building the dam was Karnataka's right and invited Tamil Nadu representatives to visit and understand how the project would benefit the state."It is my state, my right. And they [Tamil Nadu] should also know; Tamil Nadu also should know. Let them come with the delegation; I will show them, I will explain to them how it helps them," he said.He added that he had told the Centre he would bring an all-party delegation to press for the project and that the proposal had been accepted.The Mekedatu project envisages a balancing reservoir on the Cauvery river in Karnataka, primarily to meet Bengaluru's drinking water needs and generate hydroelectric power. Tamil Nadu has consistently opposed it, citing concerns over the availability of Cauvery water for downstream areas, particularly its agricultural delta districts.
Article Summary: Former Tamil Nadu chief minister MK Stalin calls for a united political response to protect the state's Cauvery water rights and the livelihood of its farmers. Stalin referred to Karnataka deputy chief minister DK Shivakumar's recent remarks that no one could stop the construction of the proposed dam. Shivak Kumar said the Supreme Court had already passed an order on the issue.

Article Title: Godhra train fire was deliberate, Sonia Gandhi's memoir claim is wrong: Ex-CBI officer
Article Text:
File photo

Belonging: A Journey of Love

Asthana says SIT re-examined Gujarat Police investigation

Nanavati Commission and Banerjee Committee reached different conclusions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

59 people killed in Sabarmati Express fire

NEW DELHI: Former CBI special director Rakesh Asthana , who led the Gujarat Police investigation into the 2002 Godhra train burning , has rejected a passage in Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir describing the cause of the fire as "disputed", maintaining that the investigation and subsequent court proceedings established that it was deliberately set.In an interview with news agency ANI, Asthana said investigators had examined different theories and possibilities before collecting evidence that connected the accused to the crime.He argued that the findings had been upheld by the Nanavati Commission, a Supreme Court-appointed Special Investigation Team (SIT) and the courts.Reacting to the passage in Gandhi's memoir,, Asthana said, "That is completely wrong, the investigation is authentic. It has been proved in the court of law. Even now, if someone is creating doubt about it, then it is for political reasons; there can be no other explanation for it."Sonia writes in her memoir, "The riots were triggered when four coaches of the Sabarmati Express were set on fire and 59 pilgrims died. The train was returning to the state capital Ahmedabad from Ayodhya, carrying Hindu karsevaks, volunteers for the Ram temple.The cause of the fire remains disputed, but the turmoil that followed spread to many parts of the state."Asked whether the doubts were being raised for vote-bank politics, Asthana said the investigation had treated the deaths as a criminal matter, irrespective of the victims' religion."All the people who died in Godhra were Hindus. And whoever's death it may be—whether a Hindu's, a Muslim's, a Christian's, or a Sikh's—death is death, murder is murder. So we investigated it as a criminal act. But unfortunately, the issue was made out in such a way that an attempt was made to investigate the case to benefit Mr. Modi," he said.Asthana said the Gujarat Police's investigation, which began with the CID Crime unit and continued until 2008, was subsequently examined in detail by a Supreme Court-appointed SIT headed by then CBI Director RK Raghavan.He said the Supreme Court constituted the team in 2008, with former Uttar Pradesh director General of Police CB Satpathy also part of the investigation. Satpathy headed the SIT in Raghavan's absence, Asthana said.The team re-examined the entire investigation, visited the site and questioned the officers who had conducted the original probe."They examined the entire investigation again. In fact, they examined us as well. We explained to them what investigation we had carried out. They visited the site and examined everything. They then concluded that they could not find any flaw in the investigation conducted by the Gujarat Police," Asthanan said.He said Raghavan and Satpathy submitted their findings to the Supreme Court, which accepted the report. The subsequent trial proceeded on the basis of the investigation, leading to convictions in 2011, he added.Asthana also cited the findings of the Nanavati Commission, constituted by the Gujarat government in 2002 to investigate the Godhra incident and the communal riots that followed.He said the commission, initially headed by Justice KG Shah before Justice Nanavati was appointed in May 2002, examined the train burning and the subsequent riots separately. Its report on the Godhra incident, submitted in 2008, concluded that the fire was part of a pre-planned conspiracy and had been deliberately set, he said.According to Asthana, around 44,000 affidavits were submitted before the commission and more than 1,000 witnesses were examined.He contrasted these findings with those of the committee headed by Justice UC Banerjee, which was constituted by then Railway Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav in 2004. The committee concluded that the fire was accidental and suggested that a stove carried in the karsevaks' coach had caused it, Asthana said.He added that the Banerjee Committee's report was challenged before the Gujarat High Court, which held that the committee was illegal because a commission under the Commission of Inquiry Act was already examining the incident. Asthana said the report was subsequently set aside."The fact is that the investigation established that the fire was deliberate. The commission established it, the Supreme Court-appointed SIT established it, and the courts convicted the accused on the basis of the same evidence," he said.On February 27, 2002, coach S-6 of the Sabarmati Express caught fire near Godhra railway station in Gujarat, killing 59 people, including women and children. The train was carrying Hindu karsevaks returning from Ayodhya.The incident was followed by communal violence in several parts of Gujarat, in which hundreds of people were killed.In 2011, a special court convicted 31 people in connection with the train burning. The Gujarat High Court in 2014 upheld the convictions of 11 accused while acquitting 20 others.The Supreme Court subsequently upheld the Gujarat High Court's verdict and dismissed appeals filed by the convicts in the case.
Article Summary: Former CBI special director Rakesh Asthana led the Gujarat Police investigation into the 2002 Godhra train burning. He rejected a passage in Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir describing the cause of the fire as "disputed" He said the investigation and subsequent court proceedings established that it was deliberately set.

After surrendering in Feb 2026 and enrolling in a law college, top CPI(Maoist) leader Thippiri Thirupathi alias Deoji, 61, is ready for his next innings in democratic politics. Deoji speaks to TOI's Bharti Jain on his demand to lift the ban on CPI(Maoist) and make it a lawful, people-centric party. Excerpts:Also read - 'From armed struggle to people's politics': Ex-Maoist leader Deoji outlines new path, seeks release of jailed cadres I left studies and shifted to Dandkarenya forests in 1984. The socio-political scenario in those times was marked by exploitation of peasantry and women by feudalistic set-up, both in urban and rural settings. In 1978, there was a big uprising by the farmers of Telangana and a declaration was made to fight against oppression and agitate for people's rights. There was mass mobilisation and a people’s movement started to give voice to farmers, women and the weaker sections. Starting from Karimnagar, it soon spread across Telangana. I was then following this movement closely and subscribed to its anti-feudal sentiment; I joined the students' Radical Students Union (RSU) to actively 'support this cause. I was arrested several times and tortured by the police. Since circumstances did not allow us to carry out our struggle in the open, I had to go underground.Our commitment to CPI(Maoist)’s agenda of seizing power through armed revolution, had mentally prepared us to face all odds and hardships. As we continued working, our resolve only strengthened...so negotiating difficult terrain, exhaustion, poor living conditions felt normal to us.There were three sources. Firstly, we would snatch or loot weapons (from the security forces); secondly, we manufactured weapons on our own. Thirdly, depending on the funds available, we also purchased arms and ammunition from the domestic arms dealers and smugglers. We have never secured weapons from anti-India, foreign-based sources in lieu of furthering their agenda.CPI(Maoist) was mostly funded by the people after we explained to them the political cause behind waging an armed struggle and the need for weapons. Also, we extorted money from outsiders who worked in our area; like tendu patta contractors and bamboo harvesters. But we steered clear of contractors engaged in construction of roads or bridges as we believe they exploit our resources. That CPI(Maoist) had massive funds is propaganda. Our policy is to raise money to sustain us for the next three years. This money is spent on people’s issues, armed struggle and propaganda; extravagance is strictly avoided. The party never had funds in excess of Rs 30-40 crore at any time. These would largely be exhausted after fulfilling needs for the current year; only a little would be carried over to the second year. There were never any funds for the third year.After People's War merged with MCC in 2004 to form the CPI(Maoist), then PM Manmohan Singh had declared Naxalism as the biggest internal security challenge facing the country. Thereafter, the entire govt machinery -- the Centre, affected states, intelligence agencies, Central para-military forces etc -- drafted a national policy to eradicate Naxalism. This unified, coordinated fight against Naxalism peaked in 2025. Security operations were only a part of this multi-pronged counter-Naxal approach, which also focused on a development of connectivity push in the affected areas. Many Naxals leaders, cadres and PLGA commanders were arrested or killed; we also lost our general secretary Namballa Keshav Rao in 2025. This weakened the CPI(Maoist) both quantitatively and qualitatively. Its geographical area of influence shrunk. We no longer had the capability to resist the security forces. Our weapons were seized. In view of our dwindling numbers, leadership, weaponry and area of influence, our movement suffered a massive setback.In Dec 2023, at an all-India conference of DGPs chaired by HM Amit Shah, consensus emerged in favour of waging a decisive battle to eliminate Naxalism. Operation Kagaar was launched in Jan 2024 and continued till March 2026.In Aug 2024, our PB/CC members met in Dandakaranya, We assessed that the decline in Naxals’ influence that began in 2018 had acquired serious proportions. We decided to disband the big outfits like PLGA, operate in small teams and work amongst the people. The cadres were incapable of implementing these decisions. It became too much of a security risk for them to move out of Dandakaranya. They had to concentrate there, exposing themselves to the forces that had encircled the area. We paid a heavy price as we could not operationalise the tactical decisions of Aug 2024.In March 2025, we decided that we were open to holding peace talks with the govt. Our condition was cessation of operations against us. But the Central govt rejected peace talks. The anti-Naxal operations continued with severity and many of our top leaders, including general secretary Nambala Keshav Rao, were killed. This crushed our movement. After Sonu surrendered, which was not cleared by PB, we could not arrest the wave of surrenders.Had the coordinated and fierce operations by the Centre and 12 states against CPI(Maoist) not been run with a definite deadline, our movement would have lasted longer as the people’s issues we raise remain relevant even today — loot by corporates in tribal areas and feudal oppression.Given the circumstances we did some rethinking and concluded that the situation was no longer conducive to continuing the armed struggle. So we decided to give up violence and come overground. We have not surrendered to lead a comfortable personal life. We want to take up people’s issues through legal means. We will now engage in people’s politics to achieve an oppression and exploitation-free society.We have been demanding that the ban on CPI(Maoist) should be lifted. This way we can take up political activity in an open and legal manner. Even the ban on our frontal outfits must go as there has been no violent incident from our side over the past 8-10 months.It is also our responsibility to secure the release of Maoist cadres languishing in prisons. This is our demand before the Centre and state govts. HM Amit Shah claims the country became Naxal-free in March 2026; so it is only apt to free Naxals who are still in jails. They cannot go back to violence when freed, as they don't have weapons. We welcome the govt’s decision to review cases against Naxals and free those jailed for non-serious crimes. But a distinction must not be drawn between serious and non-serious crimes. Govt may argue that the Maoists have killed many people, including police personnel, and that law should take its course. But this was a war and war always results in losses on both sides. After war, peace must be established. 6000-7000 Maoists are in jail; a blanket govt order must be issued for their release.Our third demand is leniency for the 10 Maoists given death sentence for the Jhiram Ghati attack case. Our demand for blanket release of Maoists should cover them as well.Our fourth demand is to extend protection to surrendered Naxals in Chhattisgarh against revenge attacks.Politics does not exist in a rigid form. Unlike Vedas, Puranas etc that are divine scriptures and cannot be rewritten, politics is dynamic. Politics must adapt to the changing times, be it the evolving national and international situation or objective and subjective conditions; political documents cannot be construed as eternal truth. Leninism and Marxism may be our theory, but the political document must be rewritten to reflect changed tactics and strategy.We will need to consult the other leaders as well as cadres of CPI(Maoist) on whether or not to join electoral politics. If the assessment is that elections will not achieve our ends, we may stay away.Since Shah had asked us to work openly and legally, our obvious choice is to do so through CPI(Maoist). We will wait and watch and take a call on alternatives if this does not work out.As we engage in political activity as per law, we shall need a network of legal experts across the country to implement our political agenda efficiently. The knowledge of law will help us to comment and correctly interpret the law to defend activities that are within the legal framework. It will also help in perception management.Armed struggle cannot be carried on or stopped with an edict or order. Popular sentiment decides its fate. Objective conditions create popular sentiment…which then takes the form of a call to the masses and congregation. This is how people’s movements are made. Nobody can predict what will happen in the future. But we are reiterating that after embracing a life in the open, we will carry out our political agenda only within the boundaries of the Constitution and law.
Article Summary: Former supreme commander and General Secretary of the banned CPI (Maoist), Thippiri Tirupathi, also known as Deoji, addresses media during a meeting with party leaders, in Hyderabad. Deoji speaks to TOI's Bharti Jain on his demand to lift the ban on CPI(Maoists) and make it a lawful, people-centric party.

Indonesian woman held at Sonauli border with alleged forged Indian IDs; NGO links under investigation

LUCKNOW: An Indonesian woman, who allegedly posed as a Kolkata resident using forged Indian identity documents and claimed to be president of an NGO assisting Buddhist monks travelling to China, was caught by bureau of immigration officials at the Sonauli border in Maharajganj district after she was unable to speak Hindi properly during questioning.The woman, identified as Rohana, was intercepted on Nov 10 while attempting to cross into Nepal. She was allegedly carrying an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and two PAN cards bearing different names and conflicting dates of birth. Her claimed association with a Kolkata-based NGO facilitating visits to China has emerged as a key aspect of the case.According to an FIR registered at Sonauli police station, the woman initially identified herself as Li Kim Lien, daughter of Li Chin Sen, and claimed to be a resident of New Tangra Road in Kolkata, West Bengal.The complaint lodged by immigration officer stated that the woman arrived at the Sonauli immigration office around 7.30 pm on Nov 10 and presented an Indian voter ID card bearing the number ZJJ2157469.The document identified her as Li Kim Lien, born on June 29, 1975, with a residential address at 8, New Tangra Road, under Kolkata Municipal Corporation, Tangra, Kolkata.However, immigration officials became suspicious when she was unable to speak Hindi properly.Her responses during questioning raised doubts about her claimed Indian identity, prompting officials to examine her passport.The passport, bearing number X2398351, identified her as Rohana, an Indonesian citizen born on Oct 20, 1970. It also showed that she possessed an Indian employment visa.The FIR states that she held an E-3 employment visa bearing number VL9126916, valid from Oct 11, 2025, to Nov 9, 2026. Her passport also contained details of a multiple-entry Indian visa issued on Aug 11, 2023.During questioning, the woman reportedly told immigration officials that she was working as president of an NGO based in Kolkata. She further claimed that the organisation provided technical assistance to Buddhist monks travelling to China.The FIR neither identifies the NGO nor specifies the nature of its activities or establishes any link with Chinese govt authorities."We are still in the initial stage of investigation to claim or deny if the woman was involved in espionage or any other activity beyond the alleged immigration and identity-document offences," an immigration official source said.According to the FIR, officials found that the woman possessed an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and PAN card in the name of Li Kim Lien, while another PAN card was issued in the name of Rohana.The FIR alleges that the woman had obtained Indian identity documents by changing her name and address despite being an Indonesian citizen.Police registered the case under Sections 319(2), 336(3), 338 and 340(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, relating to cheating by personation, forgery and use of forged documents, along with Sections 22 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025.
Article Summary: Indonesian woman held at Sonauli border with alleged forged Indian IDs. She was allegedly carrying an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and two PAN cards bearing different names and conflicting dates of birth. She claimed to be president of an NGO assisting Buddhist monks travelling to China.

Article Title: MEA reminds India's stance against Pakistan as Punjab CM seeks clearance for Lahore visit
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday reiterated New Delhi's tough diplomatic stance towards Islamabad as Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann sought the Centre's clearance to attend a conference in Pakistan During the bi-weekly press briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that requests for political clearance undergo an assessment in line with India's broader foreign policy framework."When it comes to relations with foreign countries, we have a national policy and expect everybody to abide by it. As far as political clearances for dignitaries visiting abroad are concerned, an assessment is made by this ministry, in line with its overall policy and processed accordingly," Jaiswal said."As far as our position on Pakistan after the Pahalgam terror attack is concerned, it should be amply clear to all as to where we stand," he added.This comes after Mann said his office was preparing to formally seek clearance to attend the 4th International World Punjabi Conference in Lahore, Pakistan, scheduled from November 27 to 29.Earlier, Mann had confirmed in the Punjab Vidhan Sabha that he had received an invitation to serve as the chief guest at the three-day cultural conclave in Lahore."We will wait for what they say. Political clearance has to be taken," Mann said during a press conference, noting that his office was completing the necessary paperwork to submit to the MEA.While expressing his eagerness to attend, the chief minister had also called for the reopening of the Kartarpur Corridor, which remains suspended amid heightened India-Pakistan tensions, so that legislators could visit Sikh religious shrines across the border.Under Government of India rules (Cabinet Secretariat and MEA guidelines), all chief ministers, state ministers and state government officials must obtain prior political clearance from the Ministry of External Affairs before undertaking any official or private visit abroad, particularly to sensitive destinations such as Pakistan.Following the Pahalgam terror attack and the subsequent deterioration in India-Pakistan diplomatic and security relations, cross-border transit mechanisms, including the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor, were suspended by New Delhi.
Article Summary: Punjabi chief minister Bhagwant Mann seeking clearance to attend a conference in Pakistan. All chief ministers, state ministers and state government officials must obtain prior political clearance from the Ministry of External Affairs. The Kartarpur Corridor remains suspended amid heightened India-Pakistan tensions.

NEW DELHI: A serving Indian Air Force (IAF) Wing Commander allegedly passed sensitive information about India's war plans, the operational capabilities of the Leh airbase and drone warfare to a Pakistani intelligence operative, in exchange for nudes of the woman, according to a Delhi Police chargesheet.The chargesheet, filed by the Counter Intelligence Agency of Delhi Police's Special Cell before Patiala House Court, also alleges that the Pakistani handler attempted to widen access to classified military information by sending malware to the officer. He was allegedly instructed to install the software on the mobile phones and laptops of his subordinates to extract data from their devices.The officer, who was arrested on May 30, had allegedly remained in contact with the woman between January 12 and April 1, 2026. The latest details emerge from the chargesheet filed in the case, which is awaiting cognisance by the court. Police are also yet to receive the requisite sanction to prosecute him from the competent authority.According to investigators, the officer was entrusted with confidential information relating to the IAF's war plans. He allegedly shared details of the Leh airbase, including its flight-operational capabilities.WhatsApp exchanges reportedly showed him telling the woman that the base was used occasionally rather than routinely, and that all types of military aircraft could take off from there.He also allegedly disclosed information about India's drone warfare capabilities and personnel associated with the operations.The officer came under scrutiny after security personnel at his office on Race Course found him carrying an iPhone, which he was not authorised to possess given the sensitive nature of his assignment. He was heading a classified IAF unit, according to the report. An examination of the device allegedly revealed his communications with the Pakistani operative and the exchange of sensitive information.The woman allegedly used an Indian mobile SIM issued in Gujarat to communicate with the officer through WhatsApp, despite operating from Pakistan. Investigators have also alleged that she attempted to use him as a route to access information held by other IAF personnel through the malware.Police have accused the officer of compromising national security by disclosing classified defence information to a foreign intelligence operative. He has been charged under the Official Secrets Act and other relevant provisions.
Article Summary: A serving Indian Air Force (IAF) Wing Commander allegedly passed sensitive information about India's war plans, the operational capabilities of the Leh airbase and drone warfare to a Pakistani intelligence operative. The officer, who was arrested on May 30, had allegedly remained in contact with the woman between January 12 and April 1, 2026.

Article Title: Farooq says special status of J&K ‘our legacy’, ready for any sacrifice for its restoration
Article Text:
Dr Farooq Abdullah, president of the governing National Conference (NC) in J&K

SRINAGAR: Dr Farooq Abdullah, president of the governing National Conference (NC) in J&K, on Friday said his party was always prepared to make any sacrifice for the restoration of special status the erstwhile state enjoyed in the past.In a statement issued by the party, the former CM, referring to the three regions of erstwhile J&K state, Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh, said, “people from all three regions” should extend their full support and cooperation in this struggle (for restoration of special status).On Article 370 , Dr Abdullah said, “Special status of J&K is the legacy of the NC. The struggle for its restoration would continue and that his party was always prepared to make any sacrifice for this cause,” Abdullah said.He also expressed hope that “statehood would be restored to J&K without further delay“.

NEW DELHI: BJP on Saturday urged Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and his mother, Sonia Gandhi , to return 51 cartons of correspondence belonging to former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru to the Prime Ministers' Museum and Library (PMML), alleging that the documents were taken away from the institution in 2008.BJP national spokesperson CR Kesavan made the appeal on Nehru's birth anniversary, saying the letters formed part of India's documentary heritage and should be available to researchers and the public through the museum.In a post on X, Kesavan questioned why the documents had not been returned and invoked Rahul Gandhi's frequently used slogan, "Daro Mat" (Do not be afraid), asking him to ensure their return."At least on Nehru’s birth anniversary today, will Rahul Gandhi and the Congress first family have the courage to stop acting contrary to the national interest and return the 51 cartons containing Nehru’s correspondence which rightfully belong to the country?" Kesavan said.He added that the correspondence included letters exchanged between Nehru and Edwina Mountbatten, as well as communications with other prominent individuals. Kesavan alleged that the Congress leadership's failure to return the papers would strengthen suspicions about why they were withdrawn from the institution."These letters are a part of the country’s documentary heritage and not somebody’s private property and need to be given back to the Prime Ministers’ Museum and Library (PMML)," he said.Kesavan claimed that the documents had been donated to the Nehru Memorial Museum and Library in 1971 but were taken back by Sonia Gandhi in May 2008, when the Congress-led United Progressive Alliance (UPA) was in power. He also questioned the absence of any mention of the matter in her recent memoir.The dispute over the custody of Nehru's papers has continued for several years. In September 2024, Rizwan Kadri, a member of the PMML Society, wrote to Sonia Gandhi seeking the return of the 51 cartons or permission to digitise the documents and obtain scanned copies for research.Kadri said the material came from around eight sections of the Nehru collection and included correspondence between Nehru and Edwina Mountbatten, as well as letters exchanged with former Union minister Govind Ballabh Pant, socialist leader Jayaprakash Narayan and others.In 2025, Kadri also approached Rahul Gandhi, requesting the return of the documents and describing them as an important part of India's history.The Union ministry of culture clarified in December 2025 that the papers could not be described as missing because their whereabouts were known. Culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat had also said that "no document related to the first PM for the country is missing from PMML".In a post on X, the ministry said the documents had been taken back in 2008 following a request made on Sonia Gandhi's behalf. It cited a letter dated April 29, 2008, from M V Rajan, her representative, stating that she wished to take back Nehru's private family letters and notes."Accordingly, 51 cartons of Nehru Papers were sent to Smt. Sonia Gandhi in 2008," the ministry said, adding that PMML had remained in correspondence with her office over their return.It also cited letters sent to Sonia Gandhi's office on January 28 and July 3, 2025, as part of its efforts to retrieve the papers.The ministry said the documents formed part of the country's documentary heritage and that their custody with PMML, along with access for citizens and scholars, was important.Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi paid tribute to Nehru on his birth anniversary, describing him as the "jewel of India" and saying his vision of a modern, scientific and progressive country continued to inspire the Congress.In a post on X, the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha said Nehru viewed freedom as the beginning of a new national journey and believed that democracy required citizens' participation and responsibility."India was a quest, an idea for them; diversity as its strength, democracy as its faith, and equality as its foundation," Rahul said, adding that efforts to build the India Nehru had envisioned were a true tribute to him.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra described Nehru as "a revolutionary, a visionary and a builder". She said the fact that he continued to be criticised more than six decades after his death reflected his commitment to India's Constitution and democracy.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also paid tribute, recalling Nehru's contributions to building a modern and democratic nation. He highlighted Nehru's faith in equality, secularism and scientific thinking, as well as his commitment to children's education.Nehru was born on November 14, 1889, in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. He became India's first prime minister after independence on August 15, 1947, and died on May 27, 1964. His birth anniversary is observed as Children's Day in India.
Article Summary: BJP national spokesperson CR Kesavan made the appeal on Nehru's birth anniversary. Kesavan claimed the documents had been donated to the Nehru Memorial Museum and Library in 1971. He said they were taken back by Sonia Gandhi in May 2008, when Congress-led UPA was in power.

However, he did not explicitly mention Alice Huang. She previously served as a senior executive at Megaspeed International, an Nvidia customer. For several hours on Friday, one of the world's busiest aviation networks came to a near standstill. Airports across the United States witnessed mounting delays, grounded departures and diverted aircraft after a communications failure forced the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to halt flight operations nationwide. Thousands of passengers were left stranded as airlines struggled to manage the disruption.The FAA imposed the nationwide ground stop on November 13 after communications problems affected air traffic control centres across the country. Although aircraft already in the air were allowed to continue towards their destinations, departures remained suspended for more than four hours.The shutdown, the second nationwide aviation stoppage of its kind since the September 11, 2001, attacks, affected an estimated 1.5 million passengers. More than 10,000 flights were delayed or cancelled, while hundreds were diverted.The FAA lifted the restrictions at 8:15 pm ET. However, the disruption continued as airlines worked to reposition aircraft and crew. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy warned that similar incidents could happen again unless the country's ageing aviation infrastructure was overhauled.Here is how the disruption unfolded, what triggered the shutdown and how authorities responded and why the impact could continue beyond Friday.The disruption began at around 3:36pm ET on Friday, when the FAA experienced telecommunications problems at air traffic control facilities and Terminal Radar Approach Control (TRACON) centres across the country.The outage affected multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers, including the 22 regional facilities responsible for guiding aircraft travelling between airports. Citing safety concerns, the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop to prevent further departures.The agency described the situation as a telecommunications outage and said the restrictions were imposed “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety”.At the time, more than 3,500 aircraft were airborne across the United States. Flights already in the air were allowed to continue towards their destinations, with pilots and air traffic controllers following established procedures to ensure safe landings.Providing a timeline of the disruption in a post on X, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the number of aircraft in US airspace had fallen to fewer than 400 by 8 pm ET as planes landed safely.Duffy clarified that the FAA had not completely lost its radar or telecommunications capabilities during the outage. Exceptions were also made for critical medical evacuation flights, life-saving cargo operations and law enforcement aircraft to continue operating.International flights were handled on a case-by-case basis, while airlines adjusted their schedules to manage the disruption.The FAA lifted the nationwide ground stop at 8:15 pm ET after the affected systems began recovering. However, the resumption of departures did not immediately restore normal operations, as airlines continued to deal with delays, cancellations and aircraft displaced from their scheduled routes.Transportation secretary Sean Duffy attributed the disruption to ageing communications equipment that became overloaded with data and began transmitting inconsistent information to air traffic controllers.Speaking at a White House briefing, Duffy said the system experienced intermittent radar and communication failures, prompting the FAA to shut it down."We have old, old switches, old routers. We use 1980s little copper lines," Duffy said.He described the failure as a breakdown of legacy equipment that had remained in use for decades."What went down was old, right? It was the old legacy equipment. It failed," he said."And listen, it's going to continue to fail."The communications network is used by air traffic controllers to coordinate aircraft movements and maintain contact with pilots. When such systems become unreliable, authorities may restrict departures to prevent additional aircraft from entering an already disrupted airspace system.When the FAA orders a nationwide ground stop, aircraft already airborne are not automatically instructed to make emergency landings. The restriction primarily applies to departures, while flights in the air continue to be managed by air traffic controllers using available communication and surveillance systems.During the November 13 disruption, more than 3,500 aircraft were airborne when the FAA imposed the restrictions, according to US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. Pilots and air traffic controllers followed established procedures to land the aircraft safely. Duffy said the number of planes in US airspace had fallen to fewer than 400 by 8 pm ET. He also clarified that the FAA had not completely lost its radar or telecommunications capabilities.However, the situation becomes more complicated if an aircraft loses two-way radio communication with air traffic controllers. The FAA's Aeronautical Information Manual (AIM), under Section 6-4-1, lays down procedures for such situations, referring pilots to 14 CFR Section 91.185, which governs instrument flight rules (IFR) operations during communication failures.Under these rules, pilots encountering a communication failure in visual meteorological conditions (VMC) are required to continue flying under visual flight rules (VFR) and land as soon as practicable. This does not necessarily mean landing at the nearest airport. The FAA clarifies that pilots can use their judgement and are not required to land at an unsuitable airport or abandon a destination when landing there remains practicable.If the failure occurs under instrument meteorological conditions (IMC), pilots must follow specific route and altitude procedures. They are required to follow the last route assigned by air traffic control, the route specified in their radar-vector clearance or, if neither is available, the route filed in their flight plan. They must maintain the highest applicable altitude among their last assigned altitude, the minimum IFR altitude and any altitude previously advised by controllers.Pilots also use a dedicated transponder code, 7600, to indicate a radio communication failure. According to the FAA's air traffic control manual, controllers then attempt to re-establish contact through alternative means, including emergency frequencies and other available communication channels.If an aircraft cannot safely reach its intended destination because of congestion or operational restrictions, it may be diverted to another airport. The objective is to maintain the safe movement of aircraft already airborne while preventing additional traffic from entering an overloaded system.The disruption affected airports across the United States, leaving passengers facing widespread cancellations, delays and diversions. An estimated 1.5 million passengers were affected, according to aviation analytics company Cirium, as reported by CNN.More than 10,000 flights were delayed or cancelled across the country. According to FlightAware data reported by ABC News at 6:04 pm ET, 1,913 flights had been cancelled and 10,494 delayed.At least 827 flights had been diverted by 7:05 pm ET on Friday, according to Cirium. Of these, 670 aircraft were sent back to their original departure airports, while 157 were redirected to other airports. More than 3,500 aircraft were initially airborne when the FAA imposed the nationwide ground stop, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said.The disruption also put pressure on airport infrastructure. Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport reportedly ran out of space to accommodate additional diverted aircraft and stopped accepting them.Major airlines, including JetBlue, United Airlines and American Airlines, warned passengers of continuing disruptions and advised them to check their flight status before travelling. JetBlue cancelled its remaining domestic flights for Friday, with exceptions for certain Europe-bound services from New York's JFK and Boston. The airline also warned that further cancellations could affect Saturday operations.US President Donald Trump remained "fully engaged" in addressing the nationwide aviation disruption, Duffy said during the White House briefing.The transportation secretary said he had spoken to Trump following the communications failure and that the administration was monitoring the situation.The president's involvement came as the shutdown affected airports across the country, stranded passengers and forced airlines to cancel or divert flights.Meanwhile, homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication that the incident involved a deliberate attack or posed a national security threat."There was no indication as of yet this was a nefarious attack against us," he said.Authorities were continuing to investigate the cause of the communications failure, including whether it had any connection with the FAA's rollout of a new artificial intelligence-supported system known as SMART.However, officials said there was no indication that the system was responsible. ASI, the company that designed SMART, also denied any connection.In a statement, the company said, "the current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC."Microsoft separately said it had no indication that the FAA disruption was related to its services outage reported earlier in the week.Even as the FAA restored flight departures, Duffy warned that similar disruptions could occur again unless the United States replaced its ageing air traffic control infrastructure.He urged Congress to approve $50 billion in emergency funding to overhaul the system, including outdated hardware, telecommunications equipment and control towers."This is an emergency. I want Congress to give us emergency funding," Duffy said. "This is bipartisan. This is American. I want $50 billion."He said the Trump administration had already secured $12.5 billion for modernisation but argued that additional funding was necessary to complete the overhaul.“You will have more of them unless the American people and the Congress tell us to build, and I can’t wait for that,” Duffy said in response to a question from CNN's Kristen Holmes about why the FAA was not prepared for such a failure.Holmes asked why the agency had not anticipated a catastrophic failure of this nature.“Well, I can’t anticipate every catastrophic failure that’ll happen with a TDM network, with an analog network,” he replied.Asked whether the same incident could happen again, Duffy said he could not predict the circumstances of another outage.“Is this exact thing going to happen again? I don’t, I don’t know that this exact scenario will happen,” he said.The transportation secretary also pointed to previous communication failures involving the country's aviation infrastructure, including incidents in New York and Newark.“We had this happen in New York when we had global leaders were flying in for the UN. We had a similar issue. We had an issue in Newark. It happened twice,” Duffy said. “How many times does this have to happen before Congress gives the money to fix it?”The latest disruption has renewed scrutiny of the technology used by US air traffic controllers, much of which relies on legacy infrastructure that the government has been attempting to replace.The modernisation programme includes replacing ageing copper wires with fibre-optic connections, upgrading communication systems and installing new equipment at air traffic control facilities.In April, the FAA awarded a nearly $5 billion contract to Rohde & Schwarz USA to replace up to 462 outdated voice communication switches.More than 40 new switches have since been installed, according to FLYING magazine. Federal officials have also reported replacing roughly half of the ageing copper wiring used to transmit radar and communications data with modern connections.Duffy argued that the newer equipment installed under the Trump administration had not experienced the same failures as the older infrastructure. He said replacing the entire system would be more effective than continuing with temporary repairs.The issue, he said, should be treated as a national priority rather than a political dispute."This is not one of those issues," he said. "This is an American issue."With the nationwide ground stop lifted, the immediate priority for airlines and airports is to restore normal operations and manage the backlog of disrupted journeys.However, the return to normal schedules could take time. Aircraft and crew displaced by cancellations and diversions need to be repositioned, while airlines must accommodate passengers whose journeys were interrupted.The FAA and other agencies are continuing to examine the communications failure. The investigation is expected to establish the precise technical cause and whether additional vulnerabilities exist in the country's air traffic control network.For passengers, disruptions could continue through the weekend as airlines work to restore schedules.Meanwhile, Duffy's demand for $50 billion in emergency funding has put the modernisation of the US air traffic control system back in focus, with the transportation secretary warning that further failures remain possible without a comprehensive overhaul.
Article Summary: The FAA imposed the nationwide ground stop on November 13 after communications problems affected air traffic control centres across the country. The shutdown, the second nationwide aviation stoppage of its kind since the September 11, 2001, attacks, affected an estimated 1.5 million passengers. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy warned that similar incidents could happen again unless the country's ageing aviation infrastructure was overhauled.

Article Title: 'She thought he was joking': Gujarat man strangles daughter over inter-caste relationship on Diwali; how it unfolded
Article Text:
A father named Kaushal Patel (R) allegedly strangled his daughter Saniya (L) after confronting her about her relationship.

Family claimed she died by suicide

VADODARA: A Diwali celebration with the family, a confrontation over her relationship with a man from another caste, and a remark she dismissed as a joke — a 50-year-old man allegedly strangled his 21-year-old daughter with her dupatta hours after warning that he could kill her, police said.Kaushal Patel allegedly murdered his daughter Saniya around 3.15am on Monday at their home in Metpur village of Anand district, after she refused to end her year-long relationship with a village youth. He then allegedly tried to pass off the murder as suicide, taking her body to a hospital and claiming she had died by suicide.Khambhat Town police registered an FIR against Kaushal and arrested him on Monday. He was produced before a court on Tuesday, where police sought his custody for further investigation. The court rejected the application and remanded him to judicial custody.Police said the family had celebrated Diwali together on Sunday evening before retiring to their rooms late at night. Around 3.15am, while the other family members, including Kaushal's elderly parents, were asleep, he allegedly confronted Saniya in the kitchen over her relationship.Kaushal had repeatedly objected to the relationship because the youth belonged to another caste.He also considered the man's monthly income of Rs 10,000 to Rs 15,000 inadequate, investigators said. Despite repeated pressure from her father to break up, Saniya continued speaking to the youth over the phone.During the confrontation, Kaushal allegedly told his daughter that he could strangle her. Saniya initially dismissed the remark as a joke, police said. He then allegedly grabbed her dupatta and used it to strangulate her, maintaining pressure until she collapsed on the floor.After the killing, Kaushal and other family members allegedly attempted to make it appear that Saniya had died by suicide. They took her body to Khambhat General Hospital around 5am, claiming she had killed herself.However, doctors found the circumstances suspicious and recommended a forensic postmortem. Her body was subsequently sent to Shree Krishna Hospital in Karamsad for examination.The postmortem established that Saniya had died of ligature strangulation caused by compression of the neck. This prompted police to investigate the circumstances surrounding her death and question family members.During questioning, Kaushal allegedly broke down and confessed to the crime. Police also recovered the dupatta suspected to have been used in the murder and other evidence."There was discord between them over her relationship with a man from the village," said inspector P J Bantva of Khambhat Town police station.Saniya had completed her BCom from Vadodara and was pursuing further studies, police said.
Article Summary: Kaushal Patel allegedly murdered his daughter Saniya around 3.15am on Monday at their home in Metpur village of Anand district. He then allegedly tried to pass off the murder as suicide, taking her body to a hospital and claiming she had died by suicide. Kaushal allegedly broke down and confessed to the crime.

Article Title: ‘Planned for 2 months on Instagram’: How girl, 3 friends killed grandpa over money for iPhone, bike in Kottayam
Article Text:
A 13-year-old girl allegedly orchestrated her grandfather's murder with three male friends to obtain money

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





KOTTAYAM: The 13-year-old girl got her friends to murder her 67-year-old maternal grandfather at Karuvatta allegedly to raise money for an iPhone for her and a motorcycle for her friend, as per police's chargesheet filed before the juvenile justice board (JJB).The 740-page chargesheet names four juveniles as accused - two of them aged 17, one 16 years and the 13-year-old girl. Police described it a rare case as all four are aged under 18.According to the police, the three boys entered the elderly man's house on Aug 15 night through a ventilation opening after lifting the bathroom roof tile. They allegedly stuffed cloth into the man's mouth and pressed a bedsheet over his face to render him unconscious.They then tied his hands to his thighs with a dhoti and bound his legs with a towel. They then stomped on him and beat him on the neck and head, leading to his death, but no weapons were used, the chargesheet stated. The accused allegedly stole four-and-a-half sovereigns of gold from the house.The crime came to light on Aug 17, and the accused were taken into custody the same day. The investigators said the boys showed the murder scene to the girl over a WhatsApp call. The crime was allegedly planned over two months, with the accused staying in touch through Instagram All chats were recovered from the accused's phones; information was sought from Meta for verification and the report will be submitted to the JJB, police said.Police recovered six SIM cards from the accused's phones, one of which was active only on the day of the murder, the chargesheet said. The chargesheet cites it as evidence of precise planning. The SIM details were retrieved with help from cyber experts.The case lists 87 witnesses, 98 documents and 12 material objects. Six CCTV clips are cited as key evidence, showing the accused alighting at Haripad railway station, reaching the house and leaving after the act.The prosecution has applied for the three boys to be tried as adults. The JJB will decide after hearing both sides and examining the gravity of the offence, the accused's social background and their mental state. The girl will be tried by the JJB.
Article Summary: A 13-year-old girl allegedly orchestrated her grandfather's murder with three male friends to obtain money for an iPhone and a motorcycle. Police described it a rare case as all four are aged under 18. The prosecution has applied for the three boys to be tried as adults.

Article Title: Bengaluru realtor hacked to death near Yelahanka office as wife watches helplessly, attackers flee

BENGALURU: A gang of armed assailants hacked a 40-year-old realtor to death as his wife watched helplessly in Yelahanka New Town on Friday morning.The victim, Charan Gowda, was the managing director of Dhani Properties. A native of Channapatna in Ramanagara district (Bengaluru South), Charan lived near Kogilu Cross in Yelahanka.Charan had been in the real estate business for over a decade and ran Dhani Properties, which has an office in Yelahanka New Town.Police suspect that real estate-related rivalry led to the gruesome killing. According to sources, the assailants, who arrived on two-wheelers, fled in different directions after the attack.Preliminary police investigations revealed that Charan and his wife regularly reached the office by 10am. The office is located on the first floor of a commercial complex in Yelahanka New Town."The couple arrived around 10am, as usual. His wife got down first and walked towards the staircase. Charan, who was checking his mobile phone, got out of the driver's seat a few minutes later and was following his wife when the attack took place," police officers said, quoting eyewitnesses.In a desperate attempt to save him, his wife reportedly pleaded with people nearby to help take him to a hospital.A senior police officer said the attackers repeatedly struck Charan on the head and face, leaving him no chance to escape."In less than two minutes, the attackers fled on motorbikes in different directions. By then, his wife had returned to the spot but could only watch helplessly," an investigating officer said.Charan was taken to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead.

JAMALPUR: “Your mother is dead, we’ll get you a new mother,” a 55-year-old retired railway loco pilot allegedly told his two young daughters after slitting his 28-year-old wife’s throat at their rented home in Bihar’s Munger district late Wednesday night.The accused later took the girls, aged eight and five, to the local police station and surrendered.The victim, identified as Pooja Devi, was found dead inside a locked room at the couple’s residence near Sadar Bazaar in Jamalpur town, under Adarsh Jamalpur police station limits. He alleged that the accused and some of his relatives had been harassing and assaulting her for nearly five years. Article Title: 'Ask him which judges belong to BJP and which to Trinamool', Calcutta HC tells Abhishek Banerjee’s counsel
Article Text:
Trinamool MP Abhishek Banerjee (File Photo)

KOLKATA: Trinamool MP Abhishek Banerjee ’s alleged comments that “some” high court judges owe allegiance to Bengal’s governing party, made after a reported attack on his Kalighat home last Saturday, prompted Calcutta High Court to tell his lawyer on Thursday, “Your client is very intelligent. Please ask him to give a list of judges who belong to BJP and who belong to Trinamool.”Justice Krishna Rao made the observation after additional advocate general (AAG) Bilwadal Bhattacharyya highlighted Banerjee’s comments, reported in news media, and demanded that criminal contempt proceedings be started against him. Bhattacharya read out Banerjee’s alleged comments on judiciary’s link with the governing party and its impact on verdicts.The MP, whose security cover has been downgraded by the state govt, allegedly made the comments after his house was attacked late on Saturday by around 50 people armed with sticks fitted with nails.Appealing against reduction in Banerjee’s security, his counsel, Shoeb Alam, submitted before Justice Rao, “This is the speech of a man who is exasperated and is running around for your lordship’s protection. Running from pillar to post to get some protection for his family and him, and for no fault of his but because the party he is affiliated with lost elections.Because of which, not one but six attacks have taken place… This is a clear case of breakdown of rule of law. ”Justice Rao said, “If you are facing difficulty, court is there. If not this court, then you go to another forum. It (the comment on judiciary’s alleged political link) can be taken if it’s a general public, but if it’s an educated person who is an MP and holding a good post in a political party. He is not a layman who doesn’t know what he is telling before the media. He can say anything against any person. But on a matter pending before the court…”The judge reserved his order on the plea against reduction in Banerjee’s security cover and the subsequent six attacks on him, the latest of which was reported last Saturday. Justice Rao repeatedly asked the state why the six attacks on Banerjee were not taken into account by the govt after the May 29 review meeting, which decided on scaling down his security from Z+ to X.When AAG Bhattacharyya submitted that the threat perception of all MPs would be reassessed at the next review meeting, scheduled for Nov-end, Justice Rao said, “You (the BJP govt) have to wait for six months? Your new regime came on May 10, immediately you reduced. There’s no problem. But once you have received representation (from Banerjee), why are you dragging the matter? Why are you waiting for six months?”Banerjee’s counsel submitted that considering the spate of violence since the announcement of the assembly poll results, his client feared he could be assassinated. He flagged multiple actions by the state, including removal of police kiosks outside Banerjee’s home, and alleged that the govt had acted mala fide.While the MP’s counsel said only two personal security officers had been guarding his client since May 12, the AAG submitted that three PSOs were tasked with protecting Banerjee. He clarified that Z+ security was usually provided to the CM, governor and other persons facing threats.Most MPs, he said, are given X security cover.“Banerjee’s residence continues to remain under high-grade security. He is being provided with three PSOs. Most of the incident petitions are pending. The right of a person to claim a particular class of security cannot be a matter of right,” the AAG submitted.
Article Summary: Trinamool MP Abhishek Banerjee allegedly made the comments after his house was attacked late on Saturday by around 50 people armed with sticks fitted with nails. Calcutta High Court: “Your client is very intelligent. Please ask him to give a list of judges who belong to BJP and who. belong to Trinamool.”

Article Title: 'Prove it': BJP MLA Maithili Thakur rejects land grabbing allegations against family
Article Text:
BJP MLA from Alinagar Maithili Thakur (File Photo)

PATNA: BJP MLA from Alinagar Maithili Thakur has denied allegations of land encroachment against her father, Ramesh Thakur, and challenged complainants to substantiate their claims before the authorities.Villagers have accused Ramesh of illegally occupying religious sites, govt land, roads and private property. The complaints concern the shrine of Gram Devta Tiwari Baba, a Radha-Krishna temple and a Dihbar. He has also been accused of filling a drainage channel originating from a local pond and constructing a caretaker’s room.Villager Ram Autar Mishra has alleged encroachment on his land, while Ramday Devi claimed excavation along her property’s boundary had endangered trees. Residents have also raised concerns over soil excavation along the boundaries of other private plots.RJD MLA Bhai Virendra accused Maithili’s family of using political influence to grab land. He alleged land grabbing and intimidation had become a pattern among NDA leaders and criticised the media for giving greater prominence to ruling alliance statements than those of the opposition.Rejecting the allegations, Maithili said her family had valid land documents and described the claims circulating on social media over the past two days as baseless.She said a house was being built on land known as ‘Pokhar Bhinda’, where village elders regularly gather and extend their support."I, too, only started seeing these posts two days ago. Land mafias, grabbing land, taking away the poor's rights—I'm reading all these things. These false allegations against our family are baseless. It upsets me deeply to hear that people are writing such things. If there's anything to this, ask the local circle officer.If an allegation is being made, what is it based on? Prove it... I'm very concerned that people are using such strong language—what is it based on?. .. Baseless rumours are being spread," she said.She urged complainants to approach the circle officer, DCLR or other competent authorities with evidence instead of making allegations online.Circle officer Alok Kumar said an application had been received from villagers and both parties had been summoned to a ‘janata darbar’. Villagers have accused Ramesh of illegally occupying religious sites, govt land, roads and private property. RJD MLA Bhai Virendra accused Maithilia’s family of using political influence to grab land.

Article Title: Woman buys Rs 1,755 pressure cooker, finds rice and dal remain uncooked despite 3-4 whistles; consumer commission orders refund, Rs 12,000 compensation and Rs 3,000 costs, imposes Rs 21,000 penalty on
Article Text:
AI Generated Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





HYDERABAD: A pressure cooker bought for Rs 1,755 was supposed to make everyday cooking easier. Instead, a woman in Visakhapatnam found that rice remained partially uncooked even after three to four whistles. When the same problem persisted while preparing dal the following day, she approached the seller for help. The dispute eventually landed before a consumer commission, which ordered the store, dealer and manufacturer to pay her Rs 16,755.The Visakhapatnam District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ruled that the woman was entitled to a refund of the product's cost, along with compensation and litigation expenses, after finding deficiencies in the services provided by the three parties.The commission, presided over by Gudla Tanuja, with members Varri Krishna Murthy and Rahimunnisa Begum, passed the order on October 31. The woman had purchased a four-litre deep-pan pressure cooker from a store for Rs 1,755, paying through UPI. She said she first noticed the problem when she used it to cook rice on the day of purchase. Despite allowing the cooker to function for the prescribed three to four whistles, the rice was only partially cooked.An attempt to prepare dal the next day yielded the same result, according to her complaint. She then contacted the store, alleging that its staff responded insensitively and asked her to approach the company's service centre. However, citing her age and physical limitations, she said she could not visit the centre. The store subsequently collected the cooker from her and issued a service bill for its repair. But the woman maintained that she wanted a replacement rather than a repair. The company later informed her that it had instructed the dealer to replace the appliance, but the dealer had not acted on the instruction, the commission noted.The store and the dealer maintained that the cooker had been examined by service personnel, who had even shared a video demonstrating that it was working properly. Their lawyers told the commission that the woman had refused an offer to accompany her to the service centre for a demonstration. They also argued that she had insisted on a replacement despite the appliance being in working condition and was seeking an excessive amount as compensation.The store and dealer further contended that she had not submitted an expert opinion or technical report to establish a manufacturing defect. They also accused her of threatening litigation and claiming to have connections with consumer commission personnel. The manufacturer, meanwhile, argued that its warranty obligations were limited to repairing or replacing products with inherent manufacturing defects. It maintained that the cooker had undergone operational testing and was found to be functioning properly.The commission observed that the store, dealer and manufacturer had failed to produce the warranty terms before it. It also questioned their reliance on a proposed replacement as a goodwill gesture, asking why such an offer would have been made if the appliance had no problem. The bench held that the woman was entitled to a refund as a consumer exercising her legal rights under the Consumer Protection Act, and not merely because the company was willing to offer a goodwill replacement.It also took exception to the allegations that she had used purported connections within the commission to threaten the store and dealer. Describing the remarks as defamatory, the commission said they amounted to an attempt to tarnish the institution's image and included derogatory comments about the complainant.The commission directed the store, dealer and manufacturer to refund the Rs 1,755 paid for the cooker, pay Rs 12,000 as compensation for deficiency in service and bear Rs 3,000 towards litigation costs. Separately, the store and dealer were directed to pay a penalty of Rs 21,000 to the Andhra Pradesh State Legal Services Authority in Amaravati for making what the commission described as baseless allegations about its functioning.
Article Summary: A woman in Visakhapatnam found that rice remained partially uncooked even after three to four whistles. The dispute eventually landed before a consumer commission, which ordered the store, dealer and manufacturer to pay her Rs 16,755. The commission ruled that the woman was entitled to a refund of the product's cost.

Article Title: How scrap dealer lured ex-Tech Mahindra regional head Paramjeet Dhankar to his death: 'Brother, brother, please’, 14 bullets, magazine change'
Article Text:

How past disputes culminated in Faridabad shooting

FARIDABAD: “Dhankar sahab, please come out for a moment. I need to park my car,” scrap dealer Mohan Sharma urged his neighbour Paramjeet Dhankar, a senior vice-president with Singapore-based FPT Software who had returned to his Faridabad home just a day earlier to attend his nephew’s wedding.Minutes later, as the two walked outside the main gate, Sharma pumped nine bullets into Dhankar, reports. As the senior IT executive staggered towards the road, trying to escape, Sharma pursued him, continued firing and even changed his magazine as bullets ran out. He then shouted, “Happy Diwali. I will kill everyone today.”Sharma did not stop even after Dhankar slumped to the ground. He fired at his son, who escaped behind parked cars. The incident took place just 500m from the police commissioner’s office.CCTV footage shows the sequence of events that led to the cold-blooded murder on Nov 7. According to police, Sharma, a scrap dealer, fired 14 rounds from his licensed pistol. Dhankar, an ex-Asia Pacific head of Tech Mahindra, died before he could be wheeled into hospital.The killing followed weeks of friction between the two families, who lived in the same building in Sector 21C and shared its parking area.Dhankar’s family occupied the ground floor, Sharma lived on the second, and two other families occupied the first and top floors. With four households competing for space, parking had repeatedly triggered arguments, a relative told TOI.According to police, there was also tension between the two families over Sharma’s pet dog. Dhankar’s son had objected to the dog defecating in the common parking area.An earlier confrontation on Oct 22 had further soured relations. Sharma allegedly damaged the gate of Dhankar’s house, an incident captured on the family’s CCTV cameras. The family gave the footage to police, who called Sharma to the station and allegedly reprimanded him.But another confrontation took place at the local police station on the day of the murder. Sources said Dhankar’s friends and aides confronted Sharma, abused and manhandled him. Both sides returned home at 6pm. But the humiliation is likely to have fuelled his anger.Later that evening, Sharma rang the bell at Dhankar’s house and repeatedly urged him to come downstairs and move his car. Dhankar came down with his son, Shaurya. In the footage, Sharma is heard addressing him as “Dhankar sahab” and repeatedly saying, “Brother, brother, brother, please.”The exchange turned hostile. When Dhankar suggested he did not want to continue the conversation, Shaurya began moving towards the staircase. Sharma allegedly stopped him and asked him to return. He then pulled out his licensed .45 ACP pistol, fitted with an extended magazine, and fired.Dhankar tried to get away, staggering from the garage towards the road. Sharma dashed towards him, firing as he went. As Dhankar fell outside the building, his wife rushed out. But Sharma continued firing and changed the magazine. He then threatened the family and called out to them to come outside.Dhankar returned from Singapore on Nov 5 for his nephew’s wedding in Meerut.Police arrested Sharma near DLF Chowk in Ballabhgarh the next day and seized the weapon. A case was registered against him under BNS sections 103 (murder), 109 (attempt to murder) and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy).
Article Summary: Mohan Sharma, a scrap dealer, fired 14 rounds from his licensed pistol. Paramjeet Dhankar, an ex-Asia Pacific head of Tech Mahindra, died before he could be wheeled into hospital. The killing followed weeks of friction between the two families who lived in the same building in Sector 21C.

Article Title: Curtains drawn on NCP(SP)-NCP merger after Ajit Pawar's death, received no fresh proposal: Supriya Sule

PUNE: NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule on Thursday ruled out any merger between the Sharad Pawar-led NCP and the rival party led by the late Ajit Pawar , saying she had decided to “draw the curtains” on the issue following her cousin’s death and had received no fresh merger proposal.Supriya’s remarks come amid renewed efforts by several NCP seniors to revive merger discussions and speculation over possible rapprochement between the two parties. On Wednesday, NCP president Sunetra Pawar declined to clarify the possibility of a merger between the two NCPs, saying matters would become clear at the appropriate time.“Discussions on the merger were on when Ajit Pawar was alive, and the entire world knew about them. A video of one such meeting held on Jan 17 was also circulated in the media,” Supriya said.“The day my cousin died, and following the developments that unfolded a few days after his death, I decided to draw the curtains on the issue of merger. I do not think I should speak much on the topic. It ended with my cousin’s death,” she said.After Ajit Pawar’s death in a plane crash on Jan 28, senior leaders of his party had denied holding any meetings with the Sharad Pawar-led party to discuss a merger.However, state NCP president Sunil Tatkare recently said he was aware of the talks and claimed that the merger would have taken place had Ajit Pawar been alive.Tatkare and state minister Hasan Mushrif on Thursday said they would soon meet Sharad Pawarin Mumbai, fuelling further speculation about efforts to bring the two parties together.“I will meet Pawar Saheb to enquire about his health when I visit Mumbai. He is our mentor, and I do not think there is anything wrong with any member of our party meeting him for personal reasons,” Tatkare said.On the merger issue, Mushrif said the decision would be taken by his party chief, Sunetra Pawar. “We will abide by the decision Sunetra Pawar takes on the merger,” he said.Responding to Shiv Sena neta Sanjay Shirsat’s suggestion that a third faction could emerge in NCP, Mushrif said attempts were being made to weaken the party after Ajit Pawar’s death.
